column1: # STEPS.tsv -- THE DESIGN-PLAN box-scheduler STEP TABLE (the cto, 2026-11-04, CTO-496; the design text in the shared-box skill's DESIGN section 8; Lon 2026-11-04, verbatim: "It appears COO needs help re-designing the ENTIRE FLEET system. It is a failure." / "There has been talk, and only talk, about using industry recognized ways of doing make and build load balancing and management." / "So get to it.").

# harness/scripts/test_design_box_scheduler_steps.sh reads it: --list prints it; --step N runs the step's probe (column 5, one bash command run from S4E_HOME with a 600 s budget): rc 0 GREEN, rc 1 RED, rc 2 could not measure.

# Every probe reads a live mechanism, a ledger or a plant the step builds, so a step reads RED until its mechanism exists and GREEN only while the box meets it; no probe is satisfied by a deletion (a deleted script is proven dead by the plant that shows the one law moving, never by its absence).

# The industry mechanisms each step adopts: the GNU make jobserver (one box-wide compile budget), cgroup v2 weights and quotas under one controller (sensors to actuators, floors and ceilings in BUDGET.tsv), admission by a slot of a class, a service level (SLO) the grader width answers to, change-impact test selection, and a queue whose rows close, retire and escalate by their own criterion.
